note: A palm- or fingertip-embeddable wafer-level camera module, 0.65 x 0.65 mm with a z-height of 1.158 mm (size_mm [1.158, 0.65, 0.65], z-height along the optical axis), net weight 0.87 mg (mass_g 0.00087). 200 x 200 colour (RGB Bayer), 1.75 um pixels, 1/36", rolling shutter (product page), 30 fps, analog output (AntLinx; the brief: "can transmit over 4 meters"), so a host needs an analog front end - it is not a USB device. Lens: diagonal FOV 120 +/- 6.6 degrees, f/2.8, focal length 0.175 mm, "extended focus range of 3 mm to 30 mm" (focus null: the maker states a range, not "fixed"). Only the diagonal FOV is stated; the library derives the horizontal and vertical FOV from it for a pinhole with square pixels (a labelled assumption). Over the stated 364 um image area the stated focal length makes a pinhole show about 112 degrees diagonally against the stated 120, so the lens has some barrel distortion the maker does not state. The lens model is pinhole, a labelled assumption. power_w 0.025 is "25 mW (with IO consumption)". Designed for medical use (non-autoclavable); its use in a robot hand is the planner's, not the maker's, application.
